findings.where: Article specimen: the italic pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!” (desktop-03, phone-02)
findings.fault: The pull quote is static text set in logo blue. The tile's own palette gives that blue to links and the button, and the quote sits a few lines above a real blue link. On an article page, readers learn that blue means clickable, so a large blue italic line reads as a link that does nothing when tapped.
findings.who_objects: A reader of one of Mark's articles, who taps the quote expecting a link. Angélique too: each post she adds with a pull quote repeats this mixed signal.

findings.where: Hero, the “Get in touch” button and the page's end; the nav's Contact link (desktop-01, desktop-03, phone-01)
findings.fault: The only contact route is a button that silently opens a mail program (mailto). Mark's email address is never written out, and the page has no footer, so there is no address to copy and no date showing the site is current. A visitor whose browser has no mail program set up gets nothing, and the button doesn't say it will open an email.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff on locked-down office machines or webmail, who click and get nothing, or an unexpected mail program, and can't find the address to copy.

findings.where: Hero, the supporting line under the headline (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: The line's proof ends on a size claim, “Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience”. It never says which regions Mark works in or what kinds of clients he serves. The World Bank role is a checkable fact, but the line closes on the kind of claim a procurement reader discounts. The first screen also doesn't say where the practice works.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer shortlisting against terms of reference, who judges by project kind and region. A size word tells them neither, and it leans toward the boast the brief rules out.

findings.where: Nav bar: “Articles” and “Blog” side by side (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: Two nav items name what a visitor sees as the same thing. The article specimen even calls itself “MMM Infra Blog No. 8”, so nothing tells a visitor which of the two holds Mark's writing.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor looking for Mark's publications, who has to guess between two links and may miss what is behind the other.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the principle words “precise, light, quick” (desktop-02, phone-02)
findings.fault: The principle words are set as a heading in Source Sans. The tile's own type note limits Source Sans to “the nav, buttons, labels and dates only” and gives headings to Gelasio. The tile breaks its own type rule in the section the next rounds will copy.
findings.who_objects: The designers of the layout and animation rounds, who draw inside this tile and get two answers for which face a heading takes.

findings.where: Style-tile section labels: Palette, Texture, Type pair, An article page, Motion sketch (desktop-02)
findings.fault: Like labels are treated unlike. Texture and Motion sketch have a hairline under the label; Palette, Type pair and An article page don't. Also, “Type pair” labels only the left column, so the Source Sans 3 specimen floats unlabelled beside it and reads as a separate section, unlike the other right-column blocks, which carry their own labels.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark, reading the tile as one system, who see an inconsistency the next round would inherit as the house's rule for section labels.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the “Play again” control (desktop-03, phone-03)
findings.fault: “Play again” is a button that replays the animation on the page, but it wears the underlined-blue look this tile gives prose links. In the tile that defines the house's signifiers, an in-page action and a link that takes you somewhere look the same.
findings.who_objects: The next round's designers, who would carry a link look onto in-page actions.
